summary.tldr: Gives the government new powers to secure telecom networks and protect critical cyber systems, with reporting, inspection, and penalty rules.
what_it_does: Adds security of the Canadian telecommunications system as a policy goal and lets the Governor in Council or the Minister of Industry order providers to stop using, remove, or change specified products, services, or providers.
Creates the Critical Cyber Systems Protection Act, which lets the Governor in Council designate services or systems and classes of operators in federally regulated sectors.
Requires designated operators to set up, carry out, and review cyber security programs, manage supply-chain and third-party risks, and report cyber security incidents within up to 72 hours.
Allows certain federal bodies to share confidential information for these purposes, sets limits on disclosure, and requires disposal of personal information when it is no longer needed.
Creates compliance orders, inspections, administrative monetary penalties, offences, judicial review rules, annual reporting, and a five-year review of the Act.
summary.background: Part 1 amends the Telecommunications Act. Part 2 creates a new law for cyber systems linked to services or systems the Governor in Council designates for national security or public safety.
